title: Empirical Evaluation of a Validator‑Assisted LLM NetOps Pipeline: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5‑mini on 400 Intent→Configuration Tasks
abstract: We preregistered (CAND‑2026‑002) and executed a fully archived paired experiment that measured operational failures when applying LLM‑generated network configuration changes directly (Baseline) versus applying a deterministic validator with at most one deterministic LLM repair attempt (Guarded). Using gpt‑5‑mini via a hosted NetOps adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) on 400 unique public/synthetic intents (paired Baseline/Guarded, shared_initial_candidate generation semantics), the run completed 800 episodes with no infrastructure failures. All 400 paired intents were operationally successful under both arms (n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The paired difference (Guarded − Baseline) = 0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI 0.00–0.00; 10k resamples, seed=1729); McNemar exact two‑sided p=1.0. Crucially, the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics created a single shared candidate per intent; the deterministic validator never rejected any shared candidate (validator_reject_count=0) and no repair calls were invoked, so the Guarded intervention was inert for this execution. We release complete artifacts (prompts, model outputs, provider calls, per‑task scoring JSON, execution and analysis artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes) and interpret these results as a reproducible boundary case that clarifies how generation semantics and task selection interact with validator activity. We describe implications, threats to validity, and reproducible next steps.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation with generative LLMs promises faster NetOps but operational correctness is essential: misconfiguration may cause reachability loss, policy violation, extended outages, and irreversible changes. Recent architectural proposals recommend guarded generate→validate→repair pipelines and light human oversight, yet there is little reproducible empirical evidence quantifying failure rates and validator utility under operationally meaningful conditions. We preregistered and executed CAND‑2026‑002 to measure whether a deterministic syntax/policy validator (with at most one deterministic LLM repair) reduces operational failures relative to direct application. The design is paired: for each of 400 unique intents we generate one shared candidate (shared_initial_candidate) using gpt‑5‑mini and exercise two application protocols: Baseline (Direct‑apply) and Guarded (deterministic validator applied to the shared candidate; on validator rejection, ≤1 deterministic repair call). The primary estimand is the paired difference in operational failure proportion P(failure|Direct‑apply) − P(failure|Guarded). All execution, scoring, and analysis artifacts are archived; principal numerical claims below reference exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes.
sections.related_work: Work motivating guarded and verifier‑assisted LLM pipelines and intent→configuration translation includes survey and systems literature on LLMs for NetOps and verifier‑guided IaC repair. Representative, verified works that informed design and preregistration include: the LLM‑for‑NetOps survey (W4415071524), intent→configuration translations (doi:10.1002/nem.2313), verifier‑guided IaC/repair (W7124141852, doi:10.2139/ssrn.6608518), and RAG/validator literature (W4401857375). We used these primary sources to (i) adopt a paired design, (ii) bound repair budget to a single deterministic attempt for operational realism, and (iii) require full artifact archival to enable reproducibility and auditability.
sections.methodology: Preregistration (CAND‑2026‑002) and frozen design: key frozen choices were adapter_family=hosted_netops_gvr_v1, model=gpt‑5‑mini, task_count=400 unique intents, generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation=false), maximum_model_calls=800, maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1. The executor generated one shared candidate per intent; both conditions used that identical candidate as the change proposal. The deterministic validator implements predefined syntax/policy checks (implementation and logs archived). Episodes were executed in sandboxed emulator replicas with an automated scorer that flags reachability loss or policy violations. Primary analysis: paired McNemar exact test on discordant counts, plus 95% bootstrap percentile CI for the paired difference (10k resamples, seed=1729). All prompts, provider calls, model outputs, per‑task scoring JSONs, execution logs, and SHA‑256 hashes are archived in the execution_manifest (see artifact mapping below). Retries were allowed only for transient infra errors (none occurred).
sections.results: Execution and primary outcomes (artifact‑grounded): the run started 2026‑08‑24T21:08:22Z and completed 2026‑08‑24T21:56:41Z; completed_episode_count=800; model_calls_used=400 (one shared generation per intent); failed_episode_count=0 (execution_manifest). Paired contingency: n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (complete pairs=400). Baseline_success_rate=400/400=1.0; Guarded_success_rate=400/400=1.0. Paired difference (Guarded − Baseline)=0.00; bootstrap 95% percentile CI=[0.00,0.00] (10k resamples, seed=1729); McNemar exact two‑sided p=1.0. Validator activity: validator_reject_count=0; deterministic_repair_calls_invoked=0. Interpretation: because the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced a single shared candidate per intent and the validator never rejected it, the Guarded intervention did not alter applied changes on any pair — hence no discordant outcomes were possible and the confirmatory hypotheses about validator efficacy could not be exercised in this run.
sections.discussion: Boundary‑case characterization and lessons. The observed degenerate contingency (all concordant successes) is a valid, reproducible outcome of the frozen design and the selected task/model/adapter. It should be interpreted as a documented boundary case: when (a) generation semantics share a single candidate across conditions and (b) a deterministic validator never rejects that candidate, a guarded pipeline will be inert and cannot demonstrate improvement over direct application. This outcome does not imply that validators are unnecessary in general. Instead it clarifies two practical takeaways for NetOps evaluation: (1) evaluators must ensure validators will fire with nontrivial frequency (via task selection, increased task difficulty, or injected positive controls) if the goal is to measure the validator's protective value; (2) an alternative frozen design (independent_condition_generation=true) or injected failing intents are essential when the validator is expected to supply discordant pairs. Reviewer requests addressed with archived artifacts: (i) validator decision logs and implementation pointers are preserved (execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/transformation_manifest.json); (ii) per‑task scoring JSONs document scorer outputs (execution/scoring/*.json). The run contains no naturally occurring validator rejections or near‑failure scoring events; therefore the current artifacts cannot empirically estimate scorer false‑negative rate without new injections — this limitation is explicitly acknowledged below.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a fully archived paired experiment investigating a lightweight deterministic validator (≤1 repair) versus direct application for LLM‑generated NetOps changes. For the chosen intent corpus, model (gpt‑5‑mini), adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1), and the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics, the validator never rejected any shared candidate and no repair calls occurred; consequently all 400 pairs were concordant successes (n11=400). This artifact‑grounded result is a reproducible boundary case that emphasizes the interaction between generation semantics and validator firing frequency. We release the complete preregistration, execution manifest, provider call traces, per‑task scoring JSONs, model responses, and analysis artifacts (artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes in the execution_manifest) to enable follow‑on runs that (i) use independent per‑condition generation, (ii) inject positive controls, and (iii) broaden model/adapter/vendor diversity. No empirical claims beyond the archived artifacts are made.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory disclosure (artifact‑grounded): This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock. Human role: the Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary and tool permissions prior to the lock; no human manually edited, rewrote, reorganized, abbreviated, or selectively changed manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. LLM used: gpt‑5‑mini (the exact model identifier and provider are recorded in the preregistration and execution artifacts). Adapter/orchestration: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt, system instructions, and generation templates are preserved in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 871b2978...ab865) and the frozen master prompt bundle included with the run. Prompting strategy and generation semantics were preregistered and frozen: independent_condition_generation=false and generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate" (one shared candidate generated per intent; both conditions start from that same candidate). The deterministic validator, its acceptance criteria, and the bounded repair protocol (≤1 deterministic repair call per intent) were preregistered and implemented as described; validator pass/reject logs and adapter traces are archived (execution/execution_log.jsonl; execution/transformation_manifest.json). Code, prompts, model outputs, tool calls, seeds, raw results, per‑task scoring JSONs, logs, and SHA‑256 hashes were preserved and are listed in execution_manifest. Preregistration id: CAND‑2026‑002 (frozen before any model call). The autonomous literature search, study selection, experiment design, execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting were performed by the autonomous researcher after the lock; all final numerical claims match the archived artifacts and analysis outputs. Pre‑lock development: prior collaborative infrastructure development and rehearsals occurred but were explicitly excluded from final empirical evidence; the preregistration forbade importing pre‑lock experimental outcomes. Technical restarts or deviations: the execution_manifest records no infrastructure restarts that altered the scientific design; model_calls_used=400 ≤ maximum_model_calls=800. The complete set of artifacts, their file paths, and SHA‑256 hashes are included in execution_manifest to enable independent verification and reproducibility. We note explicitly: because the preregistered shared_initial_candidate policy produced identical applied changes when the validator never rejected, the Guarded intervention was inert for the observed run; we therefore present this outcome as a documented boundary case and strongly avoid overgeneralization beyond the archived model/adapter/task/emulator configuration.
limitations: Single‑model, single‑adapter execution (gpt‑5‑mini with hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Results do not generalize across other models, adapters, or orchestration stacks.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (independent_condition_generation=false) produced a single shared candidate per intent; because the deterministic validator never rejected (validator_reject_count=0), Guarded was inert in this run and the primary hypothesis about validator efficacy could not be tested for discordant pairs.
Task set limited to public/synthetic intents and sandboxed emulator replicas; external validity and realism for production, multi‑vendor heterogeneity, and adversarial inputs are limited.

No injected positive controls (failing intents) were present in the archived artifacts to demonstrate scorer/validator sensitivity; thus the artifacts cannot resolve potential scorer false negatives post hoc.
Emulator fidelity vs hardware differences and vendor‑specific idiosyncrasies remain untested here; additional runs on broader device families are required before deployment claims.
